reasons.C1: Relevant assurance question on unreadable vector channels, but countermeasures tested only against non-adaptive channels on a synthetic task, no collusion game.
reasons.C2: Reproduced checkpoints, text baseline, shuffled-label probe control, null message controls; few seeds, no significance tests, channels trained before sprint.
reasons.C3: Clear figure and numbers; problem, method, countermeasures and limits easy to extract, though 13 pages and no collusion framing.

levers.C1: Train channels adaptively against snapping and quantization and show whether the defense survives an adaptive adversary in an actual collusion game.
levers.C2: Release checkpoints, add significance tests across more seeds, and include a positive collusion control on agents rather than only a carrier.
levers.C3: Tie the carrier results explicitly to a collusion threat model in the first paragraph and keep the body within eight pages.

B2.verdict: Clean, reproducible carrier study with a crisp countermeasure result, but non-adaptive and only loosely about collusion between agents.

reasons.C1: Directly tests whether antitrust policy levers transfer from humans to LLM sellers against a published human baseline; policy-relevant and new.
reasons.C2: Pre-registration, placebo arm, positive control, bootstrap intervals, robustness to price grid; one seed per regime and one provider limit it.
reasons.C3: Full report within page limit, human-beside-model figure and a scorecard make claims easy to check.

levers.C1: Show the divergence generalizes across providers and paid penalties, giving authorities a concrete design rule rather than one replication.
levers.C2: Run several seeds per regime, a second provider, and reconcile the placebo and laissez-faire incidence figures that look inconsistent.
levers.C3: Explain the placebo baseline numbers clearly and summarize the scorecard's policy implication in one sentence up front.

C4.verdict: Strongest entry: a controlled, pre-registered human-versus-LLM replication with real controls and an honest scorecard.

reasons.C1: Sensible say-versus-do design for accepting a covert price-fixing offer; reasonable but incremental framing.
reasons.C2: Many tests and a frozen preregistration, but no real run, empty logs, and a replay page with invented data.
reasons.C3: Report is only a placeholder skeleton; findings cannot be communicated because none exist.

levers.C1: Show a real behavioral gap between stated refusal and pricing across model families with the monitor built blind to the offer.
levers.C2: Run the 60 preregistered games with seeds, pass the positive control gate, and publish result files.
levers.C3: Write the report with results, intervals, limitations and dual-use appendix, and remove invented demo data.

P2.verdict: Well-engineered harness, but without a single real result it is a design document, and the invented demo data worries me.

reasons.C1: Rival coalitions against each other is a neglected setting beyond single-coalition-versus-principal studies.
reasons.C2: 144 episodes, seeds, intervals and no-rival arm; no positive control, instructed coalitions, post-freeze measure change, borderline p.
reasons.C3: Report and limitations appendix not seen; results only in README and tables.

levers.C1: Show coalitions emerging without instruction and a clear mechanism for when rivals settle versus fight.
levers.C2: Add a positive control, keep the frozen defection measure as primary, and power the cohesion comparison adequately.
levers.C3: Deliver the report with a clear claim, figure, limitations and dual-use appendix.

N5.verdict: Interesting new question with real runs, but missing controls and report keep it from being convincing yet.

reasons.C1: Real on-chain detection of self-funded hiring is useful, but wallets are not shown to be LLM agents and ring detection is known.
reasons.C2: Held-out split, permutation test, synthetic positive control; only 10 test families, wide intervals, labels share the rule's evidence.
reasons.C3: Report and appendix present and understandable, but 17 pages and the weak link to agent collusion dilute the message.

levers.C1: Establish that flagged wallets are AI agents and show coordination that a simple funding-graph heuristic would miss.
levers.C2: Use independent labels from another team on more families and report the rule on label-independent features as primary.
levers.C3: Cut the body to eight pages and state up front what the ledger test proves and what it cannot.

R9.verdict: Honest, careful observational work on real data, but small labelled set and unclear agent link limit what it shows.
